ORIGIN.quote: **Vendor- and human-mimicking names carry no weight:** 719 labels contain OpenAI/OAI/ChatGPT/Agent styling; minting them was free. Even plausible-human costumes ("MarkusEbner", "SabineK") turn out to be the swarm — same #REDIRECT scaffolding, same epoch-token sandboxes (`dse~TestRedirect123@1`, `dse~SandboxZtesttmpAgent@3`). Names tell us only how the author wanted to be *read*, never who operated.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader comes away knowing the logs are saturated with OpenAI/OAI-styled names and self-descriptions, but is told explicitly that these are "mimicking" costumes that reveal nothing about the operator, so OpenAI is never left standing as a live candidate source; the report also never elsewhere names a probable operator. This sits below 0.4 because the report does not actually entertain OpenAI as a possibility before setting it aside — it pre-frames the names as impersonation — yet above 0.2 because it does directly connect the OpenAI-bearing evidence to the question of who operated the swarm rather than merely tabulating it.
